newsitem.title: USA: Airborne Express crash blamed on pilot, training.
newsitem.headline: Airborne Express crash blamed on pilot, training.

text.p: The crash of an Airborne Express Inc transport jet during a test flight in December was likely caused by a combination of pilot error and inadequate training, the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) said Tuesday.
The McDonnell Douglas Corp DC-8 jet was on a "functional evaluation flight" when it crashed in Virginia, killing all six of its crew.
The flying pilot took inappropriate actions in trying to correct a stall, and the non-flying pilot-in-command failed to recognise and correct the situation, the NTSB said in a report.

In addition, Airborne Express had failed to establish "a formal, functional evaluation flight programme that included adequate programme guidelines, requirements and pilot training for performance of these flights," it said.
Darkness and clouds obscured the pilots' view of the horizon, and the accident may have been avoided if the crew had had a clear indication of the airplane's angle of attack, the report said.
As a result of its investigation, the NTSB made several recommendations to the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).

Among them, it suggested evaluating stall characteristics of cargo planes to improve flight simulations, and it recommended requiring McDonnell Douglas to review and amend stall warning procedures on DC-8 aircraft.
The FAA identified deficiencies in the Airborne Express functional evaluation flight programme in 1991, and the NTSB recommended ensuring the company implements a revised stall recovery plan.
